contentBlocks.text: This week you built a real poetic toolkit — rhythm, imagery, simile, and a traditional form — then used all of it to write your own poem. Let's review the whole set.

Quick review: ਲੈਅ (rhythm) comes from a steady pattern of sound, often rhyme; ਬਿੰਬ (imagery) uses specific, sensory detail instead of vague description (Day 1). ਉਪਮਾ (simile) directly compares two different things, a type of the broader category ਅਲੰਕਾਰ (figurative language) (Day 2). ਦੋਹਾ is a traditional two-line form where the first line sets up an image and the second delivers a completing thought (Day 3). You then combined all of these into one original poem (Day 4). Look back at your Day 4 poem: identify exactly where in it you used ਬਿੰਬ, where you used ਉਪਮਾ, and describe its ਲੈਅ in one sentence.

Excellent work this week — you now have real analytical and compositional tools for Punjabi poetry, not just a poem you wrote once. These same four tools will apply throughout this course as we study more of Punjabi's rich literary tradition.

objectives: Review and correctly define ਲੈਅ, ਬਿੰਬ, ਉਪਮਾ, and ਦੋਹਾ
Identify these four elements within the student's own Day 4 poem
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child re-read their own Day 4 poem and label where each element appears.
3. Complete the cumulative review worksheet.
4. Discuss any uncertain answers together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing the first full week of this unit — these four tools will be used throughout the rest of the course.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to point to and read aloud (rather than write out) where each element appears in their poem
Ready for more: ask them to suggest one small revision to their Day 4 poem that would strengthen its ਲੈਅ or add a second ਉਪਮਾ
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the four elements (rhythm, imagery, simile, or the ਦੋਹਾ form) needs the most re-teaching
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. ਲੈਅ is rhythm, often from a steady sound pattern or rhyme. 2. ਬਿੰਬ is specific, sensory imagery. 3. ਉਪਮਾ is a direct comparison between two different things, part of ਅਲੰਕਾਰ (figurative language). 4. ਦੋਹਾ is a traditional two-line form: an image-setting line followed by a completing thought.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's four poetic-analysis tools (rhythm, imagery, simile, traditional form) before the unit continues further into Punjabi's literary tradition, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.
